evidence: src/mail/mail.module.ts: MailModule declares providers [MailService, MailProcessor] and exports only [MailService], so the boundary is narrow and mail-focused.
src/mail/mail.module.ts: BullModule.registerQueueAsync({ name: config.get('mail.queueName') }) sets up the mail queue that MailProcessor uses.
src/mail/mail.module.ts: MailerModule.forRootAsync sets the transport, defaults and Pug template settings from mailConfig, falling back from process.env values in the same way throughout.
src/mail/mail.module.ts: queueConfig provides the inline Redis host, port, password and retryStrategy. Whether other modules duplicate these settings can't be checked from this unit.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The unit is a single NestJS module file, src/mail/mail.module.ts, and it serves one concern: sending email. It wires the mail queue (BullModule.registerQueueAsync, named from config 'mail.queueName'), the SMTP transport and Pug templates (MailerModule.forRootAsync), and the mail-specific providers (MailService, MailProcessor). It exports only MailService, which keeps the boundary narrow. Every setting follows the same pattern: use the environment variable if set, otherwise the config value.

There are a few minor smells, but none is serious enough to fail:
- The file reads config.get('mail.queueName') directly even though it already holds mailConfig = config.get('mail').
- process.env.MAIL_FROM is used as the fallback for both the display name (mailConfig.from) and the address (mailConfig.fromMail). This is more likely a configuration bug than a cohesion problem.
- The Redis connection settings, including the retryStrategy, are defined inline. Other modules that register queues may repeat them, but no such files are shown, so duplication cannot be confirmed from this unit.

The module does not mix in unrelated concerns or bypass its own abstractions.
